ARG.name: Argentina
ARG.gender marker: Source 1: Argentina, Ley 26.743 de Identidad de Género (Senate 9 May 2012, promulgated by Decreto 773/2012 on 24 May 2012) — world's first national self-ID LGR law (no surgery, diagnosis, or judicial authorization). YNA 2012.

ARG.gender marker: Source 3: Ley 26.743 Identidad de Género, Boletín Oficial 24 May 2012, https://www.boletinoficial.gob.ar/detalleAviso/primera/70106/20120524

ARG.third gender recognition: Source 1: Argentina, Decreto 476/2021 (Boletín Oficial 21 July 2021) — nonbinary 'X' on DNI and passports (first in Latin America); window-start 2018 = Mendoza Civil Registry first gender-neutral birth certificate (Nov 2018, administrative precursor). YNA 2021 (national instrument).

AUS.name: Australia
AUS.gender marker: Sub National Coverage: ACT, NSW, NT, QLD, SA, TAS, VIC, WA
AUS.gender marker: Source 1: Australia (subnational), South Australia Sexual Reassignment Act 1988 (effective 15 Nov 1988) — first jurisdiction; WA Gender Reassignment Act 2000; federal Sex and Gender Recognition Guidelines (1 July 2013); Norrie [2014] HCA 11. YNA 1988.
AUS.gender marker: Source 2: Population-weighted subnational Proportion calculated using 2000/2001 Census population denominators; see Codebook Section 3.3
AUS.gender marker: Source 3: Williamson, Trans Rights Indicator Project (TRIP), https://www.transrightsindex.org/; national legal gender recognition laws

AUS.gender marker: Source 5: Subnational sources: South Australia Sexual Reassignment Act 1988 (SA) (commenced 1 Jan 1989; superseded by BDMR (Gender Identity) Amendment Act 2016); NSW Transgender (Anti-Discrimination and Other Acts Amendment) Act 1996, Act 22; ACT BDMR Act 1997 and 2014 amendments; WA Gender Reassignment Act 2000, Act 24; Queensland BDMR Act 2003 s.23; Northern Territory BDMR Act 2004; Victoria BDMR Act 1996 ss. 30A-30E amendments operative from 2005; Tasmania Justices and Related Legislation (Marriage and Gender Amendments) Act 2019, Act 3 of 2019; Vic BDMR Amendment Act 2019; AB v. Western Australia (2011) 244 CLR 390 (HCA) clarified federal recognition.
AUS.gender marker: Source 6: Documented use: Documented: Re Kevin [2001] FamCA 1074 records that Kevin's NSW birth certificate was reissued in the male sex (c.1998) under the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act 1995 (NSW) post-1996 Transgender Act; state BDM change-of-sex registration operative across jurisdictions. Year 1998 = reissuance recorded in the judgment; earlier SA Sexual Reassignment Act 1988 certificates exist but were not pinned in this shallow pass. Medium-high confidence. https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/cases/cth/FamCA/2001/1074.html; https://gendercentre.org.au/downloads/Identity%20Documents.pdf
AUS.third gender recognition: Sub National C: Sub-national trajectory (ABS weights). Federal layer via DFAT passport 'X' policy (Sept 2011) and Sex and Gender Recognition Guidelines (1 July 2013) applied across all Australians; state/territory birth-certificate reform then ramped: ACT Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Amendment Act 2014 (first, in force March 2014); South Australia 2017; Tasmania Justice and Related Legislation (Marriage and Gender Amendments) Act 2019; Victoria Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Amendment Act 2019; Northern Territory 2019; Queensland Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act 2023 (in force June 2023); Western Australia reform pending. NSW remains the sole outlier without a non-binary birth-certificate marker.
AUS.third gender recognition: Source 1: Australia, DFAT passport policy (September 2011) — 'X' available to non-binary/intersex applicants on a doctor's letter (precursor: first X passport to Alex MacFarlane, 2003, intersex-only); 2013 federal Sex and Gender Recognition Guidelines; Norrie [2014] HCA 11 ('non-specific' registry entry, NSW). YNA 2011; window extended 2011-2013 (had wrongly started 2014 — window may not postdate YNA).
AUS.third gender recognition: Source 2: Population-weighted subnational Proportion calculated using 2000/2001 Census population denominators; see Codebook Section 3.3
AUS.third gender recognition: Source 3: Subnational sources: Commonwealth Sex and Gender Diverse Guidelines (Australian Government Guidelines on the Recognition of Sex and Gender, June 2013, updated 2015); ACT BDMR Amendment Act 2014, Act 18; SA BDMR (Gender Identity) Amendment Act 2016 (commenced 28 Nov 2016); NT BDMR and Other Legislation Amendment Act 2018; Victoria BDMR Amendment Act 2019, Act 45 (commenced 1 May 2020); Tasmania Justices and Related Legislation (Marriage and Gender Amendments) Act 2019, Act 3 (commenced 5 Sep 2019); Queensland BDMR Act 2023 (commenced 2023); NSW BDMR Amendment (Recognised Details Certificate) Act 2024; WA BDMR Amendment (Sex or Gender Changes) Act 2024. NSW Registrar of Births v. Norrie, (2014) 250 CLR 490 (HCA) confirmed administrative recognition.
AUS.third gender recognition: Source 4: Documented use: Documented use : 'X' passports actually issued since 2003 (Alex MacFarlane, first X passport on Victorian indeterminate birth certificate); issuance continued under the Sept 2011 DFAT policy extending X to non-binary applicants without surgery (Intersex Human Rights Australia, 'Ten years of X passports', 2013; QNews).

AUT.name: Austria
AUT.gender marker: Source 1: Austria, first Transsexuellen-Erlass (Interior Ministry, 1983; superseded 1996) under Personenstandsgesetz §41 — origin of medicalized LGR; VwGH 27 Feb 2009 (2008/06/0032) removed the surgery prerequisite (reform). YNA 1983.
AUT.gender marker: Source 2: VwGH Ro 2008/06/0032 (27 February 2009) removed the surgery prerequisite for civil-registry sex change; medical diagnosis of gender identity disorder retained under Personenstandsgesetz section 41.
AUT.gender marker: Source 3: Documented use: Documented: administrative Personenstandsänderung practice under the 1983 Transsexuellen-Erlass with completed changes recorded in TransX/QCK legal histories; VwGH 29.11.2010, 2010/17/0042 (Michelle B.) — completed recognition without surgery from 2010. Lift year 1983 clamps to window start. Medium-high confidence. https://qck.tirol/2023/02/23/die-geschichte-der-personenstandsaenderung-in-oesterreich/; https://www.transx.at/Pub/Rechtsentwicklung.php
AUT.third gender recognition: Source 1: Austria, VfGH G 77/2018 (15 June 2018) + BMI Erlass (December 2018) — 'divers' entry required for intersex persons with medical certificate. SCOPE: intersex-only until a 2025 VfGH ruling extended to non-binary persons. YNA 2018.
AUT.third gender recognition: Source 2: Innenministerium Erlass BMI-VA1300/0528-III/2/a/2018 (December 2018) implementing VfGH G 77/2018 by permitting "divers," "inter," "offen," or no entry on civil status documents.
AUT.third gender recognition: Source 3: Documented use: Documented use : Alex Jürgen received Austria's first third-gender documents on 14 May 2019 — passport with 'X' and birth certificate 'divers' — implementing VfGH G77/2018 (PinkNews, 14 May 2019; SBS; Intersex Campaign for Equality). 2018 era-start year retains 0.75: no documented issuance before the 2019 implementation.

BEL.name: Belgium
BEL.gender marker: Source 1: Court practice from the mid-1980s (approx. 1985): action en rectification / vordering tot wijziging van geslacht before the tribunal de premiere instance for post-operative applicants (Meier & Motmans 2020: pre-2007 sex marker changed by court; Senaeve & Uytterhoeven 2008: the 2007 law REPLACED this court procedure). Year approximate — dc low.; Belgium, Loi du 10 mai 2007 relative à la transsexualité — first statutory LGR (medicalized, incl. sterilization); Loi du 25 juin 2017 (self-ID, in force 1 Jan 2018) as reform. YNA 2007.
BEL.gender marker: Source 2: Williamson, Trans Rights Indicator Project (TRIP), https://www.transrightsindex.org/; national legal gender recognition laws
BEL.gender marker: Source 3: Loi du 25 juin 2017 réformant des régimes relatifs aux personnes transgenres, Moniteur belge 10 July 2017, https://www.ejustice.just.fgov.be/cgi_loi/change_lg.pl?cn=2017062503
BEL.gender marker: Source 4: Cour constitutionnelle de Belgique arrêt 99/2019 (partial annulment for non-binary recognition)
BEL.gender marker: Source 5: Documented use: Documented: IGVM (Institut pour l'égalité des femmes et des hommes) National Register statistics count officially registered sex changes from 1993 onward (court route pre-2007, law of 10 May 2007, law of 25 June 2017; peak 741 requests in 2018). High confidence. https://igvm-iefh.belgium.be/sites/default/files/chiffres_personnes_transgenres_registre_national.pdf

BGD.name: Bangladesh
BGD.third gender recognition: Source 1: Bangladesh, Cabinet decision of 11 November 2013 recognizing hijra as a gender category (Gazette January 2014) — government documents incl. NID/passports. YNA 2013.
BGD.third gender recognition: Source 2: Human Rights Watch, "I Want to Live With My Head Held High": Abuses Against Transgender People in Bangladesh (December 2016), pp. 35-48 — documents implementation gaps of the 2013 hijra recognition decision including the abandoned 2014 civil-service recruitment scheme.

BGR.name: Bulgaria
BGR.gender marker: Source 1: Court practice under the Civil Registration Act (in force 27 July 1999) Arts 73/76: earliest documented grant Sofia District Court 14 Dec 2000 (case 4566/2000); SCC allowed recognition 2004; repeated grants (Stara Zagora 2007, Plovdiv, Varna).; Bulgaria, Identity Documents Act amendment (2009) permitting sex change in identity documents, operationalized through court practice (notably SCC Decision No. 205/2017, Case 2180/2016, lifting the surgery requirement). TERMINATED: SCC Interpretive Decision No. 2/2020 (decided 20 Feb 2023) held Bulgarian law does not permit legal gender change — ending court-based LGR. YNA corrected from 2003 to 2009; YNR 2023. (CJEU C-43/24 Shipov, March 2026, postdates the window.)
BGR.gender marker: Source 2: Tulkuvatelno reshenie No. 2/2020 g. po t.d. No. 2/2020 g. na OSGK (Supreme Court of Cassation, issued 20 February 2023) — binding interpretive decision that Bulgarian law does not permit change of sex in civil-registry documents; procedural route effectively closed.
BGR.gender marker: Source 3: Documented use: Documented (medium confidence): Bulgarian courts granted legal gender change petitions in a substantial line of pre-2023 case law — the contradictory-but-existing granting practice is recorded in ECtHR Y.T. v Bulgaria (2020), in practitioner guidance on winning such cases, and in the 28-21 split of the Feb 2023 VKS interpretative decision that ended the practice (downgrade from 2023 is a separate matter). Year 2017 anchors to the documented mid-2010s granting line (incl. VKS-level allowance Jan 2017); earliest grants may predate this. https://hudoc.echr.coe.int/eng?i=001-203898; http://web.archive.org/web/20251009204705/https://petkovalegal.com/%D1%81%D0%BC%D1%8F%D0%BD%D0%B0-%D0%BD%D0%B0-%D0%BF%D0%BE%D0%BB%D0%B0-%D0%BF%D0%BE-%D1%81%D1%8A%D0%B4%D0%B5%D0%B1%D0%B5%D0%BD-%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%B4/; https://balkaninsight.com/2023/02/21/bulgarian-supreme-court-rules-against-transgender-peoples-rights/

BIH.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
BIH.gender marker: Source 1: Bosnia and Herzegovina (entity-level), FBiH Law on Personal Name (Sl. novine FBiH 7/2012), Art. 9 ('promjena spola') — earliest positively confirmed entity instrument; RS Personal Name law versions (27/93, 15/00) unverified (could push the origin earlier — dc flag). BLR.name: Belarus
BLR.gender marker: Source 1: MoH Postanovlenie No. 15 of 10 June 2005 'Instruction on the procedure for changing and correcting sex' (basis: Law on Healthcare 1993): Interdepartmental Commission decision triggers passport/document change, with surgery authorized only >=6 months AFTER document change (verified full text). Replaced by Postanovlenie 163 (2010).; Belarus, Ministry of Health Resolution No. 163 of 9 December 2010 ('On certain issues of changing and correcting sexual identity') — created the Interdepartmental Commission and the gender-marker change procedure. YNA corrected from 1992 (the Law on Civil Status Acts governs registration generally but does not create the procedure); window 2010-2025 consistent.
BLR.gender marker: Source 2: Williamson, Trans Rights Indicator Project (TRIP), https://www.transrightsindex.org/; national legal gender recognition laws
BLR.gender marker: Source 3: Documented use: Documented: TUT.by (2014) — ~70 Belarusians completed state-commission-approved sex/document change over the preceding 20 years (i.e., since ~1994); 64 commission permissions in the 12 years to 2015; 1-2 per year typical. High confidence for the documented span. http://web.archive.org/web/20160322160337/http://news.tut.by:80/society/399314.html

BOL.name: Bolivia
BOL.gender marker: Source 1: Bolivia, Ley N° 807 de Identidad de Género (21 May 2016) — administrative name/sex change procedure (Arts. 9-10), which SURVIVED TCP Sentencia 0076/2017 (only the Art. 11(II) rights-effects clause was struck; confirmed by Constitutional Order 0028/2017). YNA 2016.
BOL.gender marker: Source 2: Williamson, Trans Rights Indicator Project (TRIP), https://www.transrightsindex.org/; national legal gender recognition laws
BOL.gender marker: Source 3: Documented use: Documented: SERECI reported 270 completed name/sex-data change procedures under Ley 807 (21 May 2016) by March 2019; first new IDs issued from August 2016. High confidence. http://web.archive.org/web/20260712134634/https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ley_de_identidad_de_g%C3%A9nero_(Bolivia); https://www.defensoria.gob.bo/noticias/a-tres-anyos-de-la-promulgacion-de-la-ley-807-de-identidad-de-genero

BRA.name: Brazil
BRA.gender marker: Source 1: STJ REsp 737.993/MG + REsp 1.008.398/SP (3a Turma, Oct 2009): consolidated post-surgery judicial rectification of name AND sex with no public notation; continuous state-court practice thereafter; STJ 2017 dropped the surgery requirement; STF ADI 4275 (March 2018) = self-ID.; Brazil, STF ADI 4275 (1 March 2018) — self-ID gender change at the civil registry without surgery or judicial order; operationalized by CNJ Provimento No. 73 (28 June 2018). YNA 2018.
BRA.gender marker: Source 2: STF ADI 4.275 (1 March 2018) recognized right to gender identity self-declaration without judicial or medical procedure; implemented by CNJ Provimento 73/2018 (28 June 2018) via notarial (cartorio) procedure.

High confidence for 2005 instance and 2018+ statistics. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberta_Close; https://www.anoreg.org.br/site/retificacao-de-nome-e-genero-em-cartorio-mais-agilidade-dignidade-inclusao-e-cidadania-plena/

BWA.name: Botswana
BWA.gender marker: Source 1: Botswana, ND v Attorney General and Another (MAHGB-000449-15, High Court, 29 September 2017) — ordered the Registrar to change a transgender man's gender marker under the National Registration Act 1986 s.16. YNA 2017.
BWA.gender marker: Source 2: Williamson, Trans Rights Indicator Project (TRIP), https://www.transrightsindex.org/; national legal gender recognition laws
BWA.gender marker: Source 3: Documented use: Documented: court-granted changes — ND v Attorney General (High Court, Sept 2017; registrar changed trans man's ID female-to-male, Jan 2018) and Tshepo Ricki Kgositau (High Court, Dec 2017, ordered new female ID within 21 days). High confidence. http://web.archive.org/web/20240519023253/https://www.southernafricalitigationcentre.org/2018/01/08/news-release-botswana-registrar-changes-transgender-mans-identity-document-from-female-to-male/; https://www.africanews.com/2017/10/05/botswana-transgender-man-wins-10-year-court-battle-for-legal-recognition/

CAN.name: Canada
CAN.gender marker: Sub National Coverage: Sub-national trajectory (StatsCan weights). Ontario dropped the surgery requirement first via XY v Ontario (HRTO, 11 April 2012); Manitoba 2014, Alberta 2014, British Columbia 2014, Nova Scotia 2015, Quebec 2015, Saskatchewan 2016, PEI 2016, Newfoundland and Labrador 2016, New Brunswick 2017, Yukon/NWT/Nunavut 2017. Federal citizenship and passport documents adopted IRCC's 'X' marker option 31 Aug 2017.
CAN.gender marker: Source 1: Canada (subnational): Ontario first dropped the surgery requirement (XY v Ontario, HRTO, 11 April 2012); federal citizenship documents ~2015; IRCC X-marker announcement 31 Aug 2017. YNA=2017 reflects the federal anchor; under the first-jurisdiction convention 2012 (Ontario) is the alternative anchor — flagged. Graduated subnational window 2012-2025.
CAN.gender marker: Source 2: Identification of Criminals Act, R.S.C., 1985, c. I-1 (amended for gender marker); provincial Vital Statistics Acts (BC, Ont., Que., etc.)
CAN.gender marker: Source 3: XY v. Ontario (Government and Consumer Services), 2012 HRTO 726 — Human Rights Tribunal of Ontario decision striking down surgery requirement for birth certificate gender change
CAN.gender marker: Source 4: Subnational sources: Gender-marker change is governed by provincial/territorial Vital Statistics Acts. Major reforms followed XY v. Ontario (Government and Consumer Services), 2012 HRTO 726 (April 2012, Vice-Chair Jo-Anne Pickel), striking down Ontario's surgery requirement under Vital Statistics Act RSO 1990 c. V.4, leading to administrative reform 2012/2014. CF v. Alberta (Vital Statistics), 2014 ABQB 237 (Acton J., April 2014) similarly invalidated Alberta's surgery requirement; Alberta amended Vital Statistics Act SA 2007 c. V-4.1 and adopted policy 2014-2018 allowing self-declaration. British Columbia amended Vital Statistics Act RSBC 1996 c. 479 in 2014 (Miscellaneous Statutes Amendment Act); Quebec via Bill 35 An Act to amend the Civil Code as regards civil status, successions and publication of rights (SQ 2013 c. 27) amending arts. 71-73 CCQ — surgery requirement removed; Northwest Territories amended Vital Statistics Act SNWT 2011, c. 23 in 2017. Federally, Bill C-16 An Act to amend the Canadian Human Rights Act and the Criminal Code (SC 2017 c. 13, RA 19 June 2017) added gender identity/expression to CHRA s.2 and Criminal Code s.318(4)/s.718.2(a)(i); IRCC/Passport Canada introduced "X" sex designator on passports and travel documents (2017 policy, Cabinet Directive). Bill S-201 (2024) further harmonized federal documents. Sources: HRTO 2012/2013; ABQB 2014/237; Vital Statistics Acts provincial; SC 2017 c. 13; Egale Canada; Gemma Hickey case archive.
CAN.gender marker: Source 5: Documented use: Documented: provincial vital-statistics sex-designation amendment schemes operative since 1973 (BC) with completed changes throughout; court-confirmed completions incl. C.F. v Alberta (Vital Statistics) 2014 ABQB 237 (new birth certificate issued) and Ontario's first nonbinary birth certificate (May 2018, NBC). Lift from window start given pre-window statutory practice; pre-2014 instance dating is from secondary legal history (medium confidence for early years). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgender_rights_in_Canada; https://www.nbcnews.com/feature/nbc-out/gender-x-ontario-issues-its-first-ever-non-binary-birth-n872676
CAN.gender marker: Source 6: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada X-marker announcement (31 August 2017), completing federal-level self-declaration alongside earlier provincial reforms (Ontario XY v Ontario HRTO 2012 dropped the surgery prerequisite; provincial rollout 2012-2017).
CAN.third gender recognition: Source 1: Canada, IRCC interim measure (31 August 2017) — 'X' observation on travel documents (printed X field from 4 June 2019); NWT first subnational X birth certificates (2017). YNA 2017; window extended 2017-2018 (X designation operative from Aug 2017).
CAN.third gender recognition: Source 3: Documented use: Documented use : Joshua Ferguson approved for the 'X' gender observation on a Canadian passport on 31 August 2017, the day the interim measure took effect (CTV News BC, 2017); Ontario issued its first non-binary birth certificate May 2018 (CBC).

CHE.name: Switzerland
CHE.gender marker: Source 1: Civil-court declaratory action (Feststellungsklage) for change of registered sex: first documented grant Tribunal cantonal de Neuchatel 1945 (Arlette L.); routine by the 1990s; BGE 119 II 264 (1993) federal confirmation; Obergericht Zurich 1 Feb 2012 (no surgery demandable) + 2012 OFEC guidance; ZGB Art 30b self-ID adopted Dec 2020 (in force 2022).; Switzerland, ZGB Art. 30b (Bundesgesetz adopted 18 December 2020, in force 1 January 2022) — self-declaration at the civil registry. Pre-2022 court-based LGR from at least BGE 119 II 264 (1993); 2010/2012 federal civil-registry guidance ended forced sterilization. YNA 2020 (adoption).
CHE.gender marker: Source 2: Williamson, Trans Rights Indicator Project (TRIP), https://www.transrightsindex.org/; national legal gender recognition laws
CHE.gender marker: Source 3: Modification du Code civil suisse, 18 décembre 2020 (Self-ID since 2022)
CHE.gender marker: Source 4: Library of Congress, "Switzerland: Transgender persons may change gender marker," https://www.loc.gov/item/global-legal-monitor/2021-11-18/
CHE.gender marker: Source 5: Documented use: Documented: court-ordered civil-status sex changes granted by Swiss cantonal courts since In re Leber (Neuchâtel, 1945) per Swiss legal literature, continuing through the 1990s-2010s judicial route; OFS/BFS register statistics: 1,171 changes recorded in 2022 (first year of self-declaration), ~3,000 by 2024. Medium confidence for pre-2022 instance-dating (literature-based), high from 2022. https://www.bfs.admin.ch/asset/fr/24325586; https://www.20min.ch/fr/story/en-2022-1171-personnes-ont-change-de-sexe-aupres-de-letat-civil-872507694832

CHL.name: Chile
CHL.gender marker: Source 1: Judicial rectification route (Ley 17.344 (1970) name change + Ley 4.808 Art 31 registry rectification): first documented grant 1974 (Marcia Torres, Diario Oficial 2 May 1974); Registro Civil counted 729 name-and-sex judicial changes 1990-2018 (CNN Chile) — routine operation. Ley 21.120 (2018) is the self-ID reform.; Chile, Ley 21.120 'Reconoce y da Protección al Derecho a la Identidad de Género' (published D.O. 10 December 2018; in force 27 Dec 2019) — administrative self-ID for adults, judicial for ages 14-17, no surgery. YNA 2018 (adoption).
CHL.gender marker: Source 2: Williamson, Trans Rights Indicator Project (TRIP), https://www.transrightsindex.org/; national legal gender recognition laws
CHL.gender marker: Source 4: Documented use: Documented: Registro Civil data — 750 persons rectified sex/name via the judicial route between 1990 and 2019; 2,201 in first year of Ley 21.120 (from Dec 2019), 12,669 by Dec 2025. Lift from window start per the 1990-2019 registry aggregate. High confidence. https://www.theclinic.cl/2025/12/12/a-seis-anos-de-la-entrada-en-vigencia-de-la-ley-de-identidad-de-genero-12-669-personas-en-chile-han-cambiado-su-nombre-y-sexo-legal/; http://web.archive.org/web/20220727030932/https://minjusticia.gob.cl/a-un-ano-de-la-ley-de-identidad-de-genero-ministerio-de-justicia-y-registro-civil-informan-que-mas-de-2-200-personas-han-cambiado-su-nombre-y-sexo-registral/
CHL.third gender recognition: Source 1: Chile, court-ordered nonbinary identity documents (first: Shane Cienfuegos, Corte de Apelaciones de Santiago order, October 2022; subsequent case-by-case extensions; Ley 21.120 remains binary). YNA 2022.
CHL.third gender recognition: Source 3: Documented use: Documented use : Registro Civil issued Chile's first non-binary 'X' cédula de identidad to Shane Cienfuegos on 14 October 2022 after a court ruling (Cooperativa.cl; T13; BioBioChile, 14 Oct 2022).

CHN.name: China
CHN.gender marker: Source 1: China, Ministry of Public Security Reply 公治[2002]131号 (4 September 2002) — permits hukou/ID gender change after sex reassignment surgery at a state-designated hospital; evidentiary requirements clarified by MPS Order No. 478 (23 Oct 2008). Surgery required. YNA 2002.
CHN.gender marker: Source 2: Williamson, Trans Rights Indicator Project (TRIP), https://www.transrightsindex.org/; national legal gender recognition laws
CHN.gender marker: Source 3: Documented use: Documented: Jin Xing officially recognized as female (~1995, first publicly recognized post-SRS legal change in PRC); UNDP/China Women's University 'Legal Gender Recognition in China' (2018) documents the operative post-surgery hukou/ID change practice under MPS directives. Medium-high confidence on 1995 date. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jin_Xing; https://www.undp.org/sites/g/files/zskgke326/files/migration/cn/UNDP-CH-Legal-gender-recognition---China-180805.pdf

COL.name: Colombia
COL.gender marker: Source 1: Colombia, Corte Constitucional T-504/1994 + Decreto-Ley 1260/1970 Arts 91/95 — sex-component correction of the civil registry via judicial jurisdiccion voluntaria (surgery/medical evidence in practice); route operative from 1994. Reformed by Decreto 1227 de 2015 (4 June 2015, notarial deed, no surgery; grounded in T-063/2015). https://www.corteconstitucional.gov.co/relatoria/2015/t-063-15.htm; http://web.archive.org/web/20260223062311/https://www.suin-juriscol.gov.co/viewDocument.asp?ruta=Decretos/30019850
COL.gender marker: Source 2: Decreto 1227 de 2015 (4 June 2015, Ministerio de Justicia y del Derecho) established notarial self-declaration procedure for sex-marker correction, superseding the prior judicial route.
COL.gender marker: Source 3: Decreto 1227 de 2015 (Ministerio de Justicia, administrative procedure), http://web.archive.org/web/20260223062311/https://www.suin-juriscol.gov.co/viewDocument.asp?ruta=Decretos/30019850
COL.gender marker: Source 4: Documented use: Documented: 673 persons corrected the sex component in official documents in the first weeks after Decreto 1227 (June 2015) per Superintendencia de Notariado via UN OHCHR Colombia; 425 changes in 2022. Earlier tutela-route grants (e.g., T-063/2015 lineage) exist but were not pinned. High confidence from 2015. https://www.hchr.org.co/noticias/identidades-transformadas/; http://web.archive.org/web/20260223062311/https://www.suin-juriscol.gov.co/viewDocument.asp?ruta=Decretos/30019850
COL.third gender recognition: Source 1: Colombia, Corte Constitucional T-033/22 (4 February 2022) ordering the 'no binario' marker + Registraduría Circular Única v.9 (December 2022) implementing it system-wide. YNA 2022.
COL.third gender recognition: Source 3: Documented use: Documented use : After Constitutional Court T-033/2022 (Feb 2022), Dani García Pulgarín's birth registration and cédula were changed to the 'NB' marker (El Colombiano); Emma Tangarife obtained an NB cédula in early July 2022 (Infobae, 19 Jul 2022).

CRI.name: Costa Rica
CRI.gender marker: Source 1: Costa Rica, Tribunal Supremo de Elecciones Decreto No. 7-2018 (May 2018), amending the Reglamento de la Cédula de Identidad — administrative name/gender-marker change by self-declaration (implementing IACtHR OC-24/17); sex indicator removed from the cédula from Oct 2018. Instrucción 1/2012 later regularized name change; 2025 Civil Registry law adds self-ID. High confidence on the 2011-documented instance; her document change occurred c.2007-2010 (exact year unpinned). https://www.laprensani.com/2011/08/13/internacionales/69784-transexual-operado-y-reconocido-como-mujer-se-casa-en-cuba; https://www.ipscuba.net/ipscuba-net/hemeroteca/ck43-reportajes/wendy-una-transexual-frente-al-espejo/

DEU.name: Germany
DEU.gender marker: Source 1: Germany, Transsexuellengesetz (TSG, BGBl. I 1980 S. 1654, adopted 10 September 1980, in force 1 Jan 1981) — court-based LGR. Replaced by the Selbstbestimmungsgesetz (SBGG, Bundestag 12 April 2024, in force 1 November 2024) — self-ID reform, not a reversal. YNA 1980 (adoption).
DEU.gender marker: Source 2: BVerfG Beschluss vom 11. Januar 2011, 1 BvR 3295/07 (BVerfGE 128, 109) — Federal Constitutional Court ruled the TSG sterilization requirement unconstitutional. https://www.bundesverfassungsgericht.de/SharedDocs/Entscheidungen/DE/2011/01/rs20110111_1bvr3295
DEU.gender marker: Source 3: Selbstbestimmungsgesetz (SBGG) vom 19. Juni 2024, BGBl. 2024 I Nr. 206 — substantive reform replacing the TSG with self-declaration regime, in force 1 November 2024. Documents the 2024 transition; Gender_Change_Requirement field captures the pre-2024 Medical/Psychological regime throughout the panel window. https://www.recht.bund.de/bgbl/1/2024/206/regelungstext.pdf
DEU.gender marker: Source 4: Williamson, Trans Rights Indicator Project (TRIP), https://www.transrightsindex.org/
DEU.gender marker: Source 5: Documented use: Documented: TSG in force 1981-2024 with >22,000 completed Personenstandsänderungen ('grosse Lösung') over its life; court statistics on TSG proceedings obtainable via FragDenStaat FOI; 22,000+ entries changed in first year of SBGG (Nov 2024+). High confidence. https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transsexuellengesetz; https://fragdenstaat.de/en/request/statistische-angaben-zu-verfahren-nach-dem-transsexuellengesetz/
DEU.third gender recognition: Source 1: Germany, PStG amendment (adopted by the Bundestag 14/18 December 2018, in force 1 January 2019) — 'divers' entry (intersex, medical certificate; SBGG 2024 extended self-ID), implementing BVerfG 1 BvR 2019/16 (10 October 2017), which mandated but did not itself enable registration. YNA corrected from 2017 to 2018 (operative instrument); window trimmed to 2018.
DEU.third gender recognition: Source 2: Bundesverfassungsgericht, Beschluss 1 BvR 2019/16 of 10 October 2017 — held the binary civil-status register unconstitutional under Art. 2(1) and 3(3) GG, mandating creation of the "divers" option implemented by 2018 PStG amendment.
DEU.third gender recognition: Source 3: Documented use: Documented use : 69 persons registered 'divers' by May 2019 per parliamentary inquiry reported by ARD; 256 with divers/no entry during 2019; Zensus 2022 counted 969 'divers' entries (LSVD; Destatis; regionalHeute.de). 2018 era-start year retains 0.75: 'divers' option in force only from 22 Dec 2018, first documented registrations 2019.

EST.name: Estonia
EST.gender marker: Source 1: Estonia, Regulation of the Minister of Social Affairs No. 32 of 7 May 1999 ('Soovahetuse arstlike toimingute ühtsed nõuded') + Vital Statistics Registration Act Ch. 31 — medicalized LGR (expert committee, HRT, 2-year wait). Never formally replaced. YNA 1999.

High confidence. https://feministeerium.ee/en/how-the-state-treats-transgender-people/

FIN.name: Finland
FIN.gender marker: Source 1: KHO 1988-A-46 (Supreme Administrative Court) + ensuing Population Register Centre / maistraatti practice: personal identity code changed on medical documentation (diagnosis + infertility evidence); practice described in STM 2000:2 and HE 56/2001; Trans Act 563/2002 standardized it.; Finland, Laki transseksuaalin sukupuolen vahvistamisesta (Act 563/2002, adopted by Parliament 28 June 2002, in force 1 Jan 2003) — first Finnish LGR statute (required infertility/sterilization); replaced by the self-ID Laki sukupuolen vahvistamisesta (295/2023, in force 3 April 2023). FIN.gender marker: Source 2: Laki sukupuolen vahvistamisesta 295/2023 (Translaki / Trans Act, adopted by Eduskunta 1 February 2023; in force 3 April 2023) — substantive reform replacing prior surgery and sterilization requirements with self-declaration for adults. FRA.name: France
FRA.gender marker: Source 1: France, Loi n° 2016-1547 du 18 novembre 2016 (Art. 56-II; Code civil Arts. 61-5 à 61-8) — demedicalized court procedure. Window-start 1992 anchored by Cour de cassation Ass. plén., 11 déc. 1992 (nos. 91-11.900, 91-12.373), establishing post-surgical case-law LGR after B. v France (ECtHR 1992). YNA 1992 anchors the origin instrument (Ass. plen. 11 dec. 1992 case-law route, per the GMC origin convention); Loi 2016-1547 is the demedicalizing reform (YLC 2016).

GBR.name: United Kingdom
GBR.gender marker: Source 1: United Kingdom, Gender Recognition Act 2004 (Royal Assent 1 July 2004, in force 4 April 2005) — GRC via Gender Recognition Panel, no surgery. No LGR pre-2004 (Corbett v Corbett 1970; Goodwin v UK, ECtHR 2002, forced reform). For Women Scotland v Scottish Ministers [2025] UKSC 16 interprets the Equality Act 2010 only — does NOT repeal or amend the GRA; no reversal. YNA 2004.
GBR.gender marker: Source 2: Williamson, Trans Rights Indicator Project (TRIP), https://www.transrightsindex.org/; national legal gender recognition laws

GEO.name: Georgia
GEO.gender marker: Source 1: Georgia, Civil Status Acts Law (adopted 20 December 2011, in force 2012) — gender-marker change with medical certification (surgery-requirement ambiguity condemned in A.D. and Others v Georgia, ECtHR App. 57864/17, 1 Dec 2022). REVERSED: Law on Family Values and Protection of Minors (adopted by Parliament 17 September 2024; signed by the Speaker 3 October 2024 after the President refused) BANS gender-marker change on all state documents. YNR 2024; active through 2023.
GEO.gender marker: Source 3: Counter-evidence: ECtHR, A.D. and Others v. Georgia (no. 57864/17, judgment 1 Dec 2022): although the right to change sex in civil-status records existed since 1998, the Court found 'not apparently one single case of successful legal gender recognition' in Georgia; the law never specified the terms/conditions, leaving authorities excessive discretion and making recognition impossible in practice. WISG documented the FIRST successful recognition on 25 March 2021 — c.21 months BEFORE the judgment. Sources: https://hudoc.echr.coe.int/fre?i=001-221237; https://www.wisg.org/en/news/detail/324/First-time-in-Georgia-trans-person's-gender-has-been-legally-recognised; https://ehrac.org.uk/en_gb/court-says-georgia-must-establish-clear-procedures-on-legal-gender-recognition-and-finds-existing-approach-breached-trans-citizens-rights-ghviniashvili/

_meta.title: Legal gender recognition: can trans people change the sex on their official documents, and on what conditions?
_meta.what: For 195 countries, whether national (or sub-national) law lets a person change the legal sex/gender marker on official documents, and what it requires as of 2025: Self-ID (own declaration), Court Order, Medical/Psychological evaluation, Medical Diagnosis, Surgery, Surgery+Sterilization, or "No Legal Route". "No legal gender change coded" = Velasco found no legal route. not_coded_note_gender_marker = the note Velasco left on a placeholder row explaining why no route was coded (8 countries; its requirement field is not a coded value). Proportion = share of the population covered (below 1 when only some regions allow it). Each record keeps all of Velasco's fields: year of adoption, sub-national coverage, enforcement evidence, data confidence and up to 12 cited legal sources; plus the year-by-year history since 1991 and the third-gender recognition row.
